mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the negative correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1.2M for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.2% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism is not robust during periods of strong wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 101 for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease of at least 0.25 percentage points in the federal funds rate and a month-over-month increase in real savings (RSAFS) above $50 billion signals a liquidity injection into the banking system, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops >= 0.25pp AND RSAFS > $50B increase MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero during triggered events (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index above 3.5% combined with a concurrent decline in real personal income (PAYEMS) signals inflationary pressure with stagnant real wages, which erodes consumer purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when oil prices spike exogenously.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 3.8% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which correlates with higher construction-related equity outperformance and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month +5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero during triggered housing recoveries (t-test p > 0.05).
